title: context-synthesis-notebook-pranav-mitra-2029-03
content:
Quick purpose: capture raw impressions and experimental ideas from a 3-day sprint on context synthesis and long-window economy. Not polished; meant to seed reproducible experiments and a short internal 1-pager.

Top-level takeaway summary:
- Context synthesis (explicitly compressing and reconstructing long context) feels promising for high-throughput sessions where token cost dominates. The best tradeoffs are still workload dependent: instruction-heavy dialogs vs. retrieval-augmented long docs.
- Two orthogonal knobs: lossy semantic compression (summarize/latent projection) and selective KV-preservation (retain verbatim spans for entities/qa). Combining both appears better than either alone.
- Operationally, implementation complexity grows with read-modify-write semantics for KV cache; plan for simple fallbacks and strong validation tests.

Papers skimmed and my notes (short-form):
1) "Progressive Context Bottlenecks" (arXiv 2901.01234)
- Idea: pipeline that iteratively compresses prior segments into a compact prefix representation, plus small residuals.
- Methods: contrastive objective for reconstruction + aux QA loss to preserve downstream task signal.
- Empirical: claims 3-4x token reduction with <2% QA accuracy drop on their benchmarks.
- My read: promising, but benchmarks were synthetic (Wikipedia/QA). Need to test on our user session traces (chat + code).
- Quick experiment: run their compressor on 500 Redwood-hosted chat sessions (sample) and measure: token-savings, latency added for compression, downstream generation divergence (perplexity + eval on prompt-based checks).

2) "Selective KV Anchoring" (conference poster, NeurIPS 2028)
- Idea: don't compress everything; anchor small verbatim KV slices for named entities, code tokens, and numeric tables.
- Heuristic selection uses entity recognition + token-frequency thresholds.
- Ops note: anchors make rollbacks easier when hallucination detected, and can be cached separately for fast access.
- My read: anchors are a nice pragmatic middle-ground. Combine with a small LRU eviction policy by relevance score.

3) "Latent-Bridge Retrieval" (ICLR 2029 workshop notes)
- Idea: use short latent vectors to represent prior chunks and retrieve compressed latents with approximate nearest neighbor; reconstruct with a small decoder.
- Concern: extra decoder adds compute; but decoder is tiny (few M params) so might be cost-effective compared to continuing large model generation.
- Measure: wall-clock vs token-cost tradeoff on batch workloads.

Practical experiment plan (concrete steps):
- Dataset: 1k recent multi-turn sessions from hosted-api (anonymized), stratified by length, domain (support / product / code) and user tier.
- Baselines: naive window-truncate (last N tokens), prefix-summarize (static summary every X tokens), progressive-bottleneck (paper1 reimpl), selective-anchors (paper2 heuristics).
- Metrics: token-savings, end-to-end latency (including compression/decompression), quality deltas: automated QA accuracy, instruction-following failure rate, edit-distance on critical spans (entities/code blocks).
- Safety checks: human spot-checks on hallucination triage; ensure compression doesn't remove safety prompts or legal text.

Prototype engineering notes:
- Lightweight compressor should be a separate microservice with sync API: compress(session_id, chunks[]) -> compressed_blob + metadata (anchors list). Decompression returns reconstructed prefix. Keep metadata explicit to avoid silent data loss.
- KV cache: represent anchors as (key_id, raw_tokens, meta). Store in Redis-like store keyed by session_id; compressed_blob can be stored in S3.
- Canary flow: default to noop compressor for first week, then roll out per-route sampling. Add deterministic seeds for compressor to make debugging easier.

Open questions to triage in follow-up meetings:
- Latent vs text compression: when is decoder compute cheaper than running the full LLM? Need cost model: decoder_ms * infra_cost vs saved_gen_tokens * token_cost.
- How to version compressors and ensure reproducibility for customer audits? Need schema for compressed_blob and migration plan.
- Failure modes: what errors should trigger automatic fallbacks? e.g., reconstruction confidence < 0.7 -> bypass compressor.

Small reproducibility checklist for initial sprint:
- create dataset export job (anonymize + redact) -> S3 prefix: s3://redwood-inference-sandbox/ps-mitra/context-synth/
- hook up a minimal compressor (pooled LSTM-summarizer or tiny transformer) to compare with simple extractive summarizer (TextRank).
- instrument metrics in Console: token_savings, compression_ms, decompress_ms, qa_accuracy_delta.

Notes from hallway conversation (fuzzy):
- Lina: suggested adding 'pinned anchors' for enterprise customers (legal transcripts that must be preserved verbatim). Good idea for Private deployments.
- Devin: asked about eval gating for Dedicated where latency SLOs are strict; suggested progressive compression only for best-effort tiers.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- [Pranav] Build dataset export and baseline extractive summarizer + metrics instrumentation. Target: POC demo by 2029-03-18.
- [Lina] Draft policy for anchor retention and schema for anchor metadata. Due 2029-03-12.
- [Devin] Cost-model draft comparing tiny-decoder vs token-cost break-even. Due 2029-03-15.

Random loose thoughts to keep: 
- Might exploit model distillation: distill the compressor from the large LLM used in-host so compressors better preserve signal relevant to that generation distribution.
- Consider user-visible UX: show a short generated "context summary" to end-users for transparency in long sessions. Could reduce confusion when the model forgets old specifics.

References and links I skimmed this sprint (copy/paste):
- Progressive Context Bottlenecks (arXiv): https://arxiv.org/abs/2901.01234
- Selective KV Anchoring (NeurIPS poster): internal slide link in CON-1882
- Latent-Bridge Retrieval (ICLR workshop notes): https://iclr.cc/2029/notes/latent-bridge
- Internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/context-synthesis-experiments/pull/42

End of raw notes. Intend to convert to a short 1-pager by 2029-03-10 and share with Applied ML sync.
